newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NOLAN SAYS SABRES PULLED CONTRACT OFFER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NOLAN SAYS SABRES PULLED CONTRACT OFFER.

text.p: The National Hockey League Coach of the Year may be looking for work after Ted Nolan said the Buffalo Sabres had pulled their contract offer.

Nolan, who guided the overachieving Sabres to the Northeast Division title this past season, told a radio station Monday that the club's new general manager, Darcy Regier, had rescinded a one-year contract offer.

Nolan rejected the one-year offer last Thursday, expecting that to signal the start of contract negotiations. But he told WBEN Radio in Buffalo from his home in Sault Ste Marie, Canada, that Regier flew to his house not to negotiate but to break the news that the offer was off the table.
"I'm a pretty good optimist and I thought maybe today we could work something out," Nolan said.
"I was keeping that hope, but it didn't work out. I'm disappointed, but that's life," added Nolan, who said the conversation lasted about five minutes.

"Darcy's the general manager of this hockey club and he told me it was his decision and his decision only, and I have to take his word for it. He came to the conclusion that I would not be his coach and so be it."

Regier came over from the New York Islanders in the off-season to replace John Muckler, who had clashed with Nolan throughout the season. When Muckler was fired it appeared Nolan had won that power struggle.

Regier said last week the offer was for just one season because he wanted to make sure he and Nolan could work together, while Nolan obviously felt he deserved a longer deal after winning the division.

"The fans in Buffalo have been sensational to me and I've enjoyed my time in Buffalo these two years," said Nolan, less than two weeks after being honoured with the Jack Adams Award as the NHL's coach of the year.

Nolan, the 14th coach in team history, compiled a 73-72-19 record in two seasons with the Sabres. Buffalo went 40-30-12 this season and reached the second round of the playoffs, losing in five games to the Philadelphia Flyers.
But Nolan also had his differences with the team's star goaltender and NHL Most Valuable Player Dominik Hasek, who last week publicly criticised the coach, possibly contributing to Regier's decision.
The Flyers, Calgary Flames and Mighty Ducks of Anaheim all are currently looking for coaches.
